SECTION 1: The provisions of Sections 140, 142, 143, 144, 145, 146
and 170 of Law No. 2012/001 of 19 April 2012 relating to the Electoral
Code, are amended and supplemented as follows:
"CHAPTER VI
OATH TAKING
m
SECTION 140 (new): (1) The President-elect shall assume office once
he takes the oath within no more than 15 (fifteen) days of the
proclamation of the results by the Constitutionalc Council.
(2) He shall take oath of offic.e before the Cameroonian
c
people in the presence of Members of Parliament, the Constitutional
Council and the Supreme Court meeting in solemn session in the
r
manner and words prescribed hereinunder:
p
(a) The President of the National Assembly shall administer the oath
.
following a short address which he shall conclude in the following
w
established form:
w
"Mr President-elect of the Republic,
Do you pledge yourself on your honour to faithfully perform the duties
w
entrusted to you by the people, and do you solemnly swear before Gad
and al/ men to devote al/ your efforts to preserving, protecting and
defending the Constitution and the laws of the Republic of Cameroon, to
watch over the commonwealth of the Nation, and to uphold and defend
the unity, integrity and independence of the Cameroon Fatherland?"
(b)
The President-elect, standing, raising his right hand and facing
the Members of Parliament, the Constitutional Council and the Supreme
Court shall pledge himself by answering:
"I DO SO SWEAR."

CHAPTER VII
VACANCY OF THE OFFICE OF PRESIDENT OF THE REPUBLIC
SECTION 142 (new): (1) Where the office of President of the
Republic becomes vacant for any reason whatsoever, the Vice-President
shall complete the term of office of the President of the Republic.
m
(2) (a) The Vice-President shall assume office once he takes
the oath of office before the Cameroonian people in the presence of
c
Members of Parliament, the Constitutional Council and the Supreme
Court meeting in solemn session. .
c
(b) The form of the oath shall be as follows:

men to devote al/ your efforts to preserving, protecting and defending the
Constitutwion and the laws of the Republic of Cameroon, to watch over the
commonwealth of the Nation, and to uphold and defend the unity,
integrity and independence of the Cameroon Fatherland?"
w

powers, the powers of the interim President of the Republic shall be
exercised as of right by the President of the Senate. Where the latter is

(4) ln the case referred to in (3) above, a poll for the election

(5) The interim President of the Republic, that is, the
President of the Senate or his Vice, may neither amend the Constitution
m
nor reshuffle the Government. He may not organize a referendum or be
a candidate in the Presidential election. However, in case of necessity
related to the organization of the presidenctial election, the acting
President of the Republic may, upon consultation with the Constitutional
.
Council, reshuffle the Government.
c
SECTION 143 (new): (1) ln the event of resignation of the President of
r
the Republic, he shall so inform the nation in a message.
p
(2) The resigning President of the Republic shall then tender
.
his resignation to the President of the Constitutional Council and the
w
Vice-President of the Republic.
(3) The message referred to in (1) above shall be published
w
according to the procedure of urgency, and inserted in the Official
Gazette in English and French.
w
SECTION 144 (new): (1) Where the office of the President of the
Republic becomes vacant as a result of death, the Vice-President of the
Republic shall assume office once he takes the oath as provided for in
Section 142(2) above.
SECTION 145 (new): (1) The permanent unavailability of the
President of the Republic shall be ascertained by a majority of 2/3 (two
thirds) of the members of the Constitutional Council.
(2) Such unavailability shall be referred to the
